# Finance summary: working capital by service level

*Generated by `python -m inventory.finance` from the 2011 backtest. Do not edit by hand.*

Client: UK online gift retailer (UCI Online Retail II). Current service level: **95%**.

## What the money says

Moving from 95% to **98%** ties up £5,097 more cash in stock on average. It adds £1,203 a year in holding cost, recovers £2,093 of lost margin, and saves **£890 a year** overall.

Each £1 of extra stock returns about 17% a year after its holding cost.

The next step, to 99%, would tie up £3,465 more for £51 a year: 1.5% on the extra cash, below finance's 10% hurdle. That is where extra stock stops paying for itself.

## Each step up, judged as an investment

Finance's hurdle: extra stock must save at least 10% of the extra cash a year, after its holding cost.

| Step | Extra cash in stock | Net saving / yr | Return on extra cash | Clears hurdle |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 80% → 90% | £5,568 | £2,545 | 45.7% | yes |
| 90% → 95% | £4,710 | £965 | 20.5% | yes |
| 95% → 98% | £5,097 | £890 | 17.5% | yes |
| 98% → 99% | £3,465 | £51 | 1.5% | no |

## Assumptions finance is asked to sign off

| Assumption | Value | Source |

| Unit cost | 60% of median selling price | config/client_settings.json |
| Holding cost, including cost of capital | 25% of stock value per year | config/client_settings.json |
| Trading days per year | 302 | config/client_settings.json |
| Minimum return on extra stock | 10% a year | config/client_settings.json |
| Supplier lead times | 5-20 trading days, 0 set by the client | config/client_settings.json |
| Lost sale | Unmet demand is lost, valued at selling price minus unit cost | Model |
| Demand | Real 2011 daily sales; policies set from 2010 only | UCI Online Retail II |

Working capital is the average value of stock on hand at unit cost. The holding rate already includes the cost of tying up that cash, so it is not counted twice.
